title: Producing Your Own Carrot Seeds
summary: Learn how to select and produce your own carrot seeds: discover the difference between annual tropical/oriental carrots and biennial carrots, master root selection digging to pick the best sweet taproots, and harvest beautiful primary dry umbels for easy threshing and debearding.

pages.title: Welcome to carrot seed production
pages.text:
The carrot is a crunchy, sweet root rich in vitamins, highly valued by households and profitable at the market.  
Producing your own carrot seeds requires method: to know if a carrot is good, you must first dig it up and look underground!  
Discover all professional practices to harvest abundant seeds adapted to your local terroir.
pages.illustration_description: Medium shot in a market garden: A farmer pulls out a beautiful conical orange carrot with lush feathery foliage.

pages.title: What we will learn
pages.text:
In this practical lesson, we will cover 5 key steps:
1. Discovering the umbel flower and cross-pollination risk with wild carrot.
2. Prioritizing varieties adapted to hot climates (annual/tropical types).
3. The seed saver's secret gesture: digging up roots, tasting the tip, and selecting the best.
4. Replanting mother roots and staking flower stalks.
5. Harvesting primary umbels, rubbing spiny seeds to debeard them and preserving them for 5 years.

pages.title: Step 1: The umbel and cross-pollination
pages.text:
The carrot inflorescence is shaped like a beautiful umbrella made of hundreds of small white flowers. This is called an **umbel**.  
In each tiny flower, male organs produce pollen before the female organ is ready.  
The flower cannot self-pollinate alone: it relies entirely on visiting insects (flies, small bees, beetles). It is a **cross-pollinating (allogamous)** plant.
pages.illustration_description: Close up of a carrot umbel with pollinators.

pages.title: Beware of wild carrot danger!
pages.text:
⚠️ Cultivated carrots readily cross with **wild carrot** growing along roadsides and fallow fields.  
Wild carrot has dominant genes: if it fertilizes your carrot, the following year your roots will turn hard, white, fibrous, and inedible!  
To distinguish them: wild carrot umbels almost always have a **tiny black or dark purple flower right in the center**.  
✅ Remove all wild carrots within a **500 m to 1 km** radius around your seed plot.
pages.illustration_description: Side by side comparison of cultivated and wild carrot umbels.

pages.title: Step 2: Varieties adapted to hot climates
pages.text:
There are two main types of carrots:
- **Western carrots** (such as Nantes): require cold winter conditions to flower. In tropical lowlands, they rarely set seed!
- **Oriental / tropical carrots** (Kuroda, New Kuroda types, Asian varieties): very vigorous, heat tolerant, flowering in their first season without heavy cold.  
✅ Always choose tropical varieties suited to hot climates for successful seed production.
pages.illustration_description: Illustrated comparison between temperate and tropical carrots.

pages.title: Step 3: Root selection digging
pages.text:
To produce high quality seeds, do not leave roots in the ground blindly.  
At maturity, gently dig up 30 to 50 healthy carrots.  
Carefully inspect each root:
- Keep straight, uniform, deep-orange carrots.
- Eliminate branched, split, or pale roots.
- Cut the very tip of the root to taste sweetness and crunchiness.
- Dip the cut tip in clean wood ash to prevent rot.
pages.illustration_description: Farmer examining dug up carrot roots.

pages.title: Step 4: Replanting mother roots
pages.text:
Selected roots are called **mother roots**.  
1. Trim the foliage back to 5 cm above the crown.
2. Replant them in fertile, well-drained soil spaced 50 cm apart.
3. Water well after transplanting.
4. As the flower stalk grows up to 1.5 m, stake it firmly to resist strong winds.

pages.title: Flowering and ripening of umbels
pages.text:
The main central umbel (primary umbel) blooms first and produces the largest, most vigorous seeds.  
Secondary umbels follow on side branches.  
As seeds mature, the flat white umbel curls inwards like a bird's nest and turns from green to light brown.

pages.title: Harvesting dry umbels
pages.text:
Harvest on a dry, sunny morning when umbels have turned crisp and brown.  
Cut the primary umbels with 5 cm of stem attached.  
Place them in a dry, ventilated cloth bag or basket in the shade for a few days to complete drying.
pages.illustration_description: Harvesting brown dry umbels with shears.

pages.title: Debearding and threshing carrot seeds
pages.text:
Carrot seeds are covered with tiny hooked hairs that make them cling together!  
To obtain easy-to-sow individual seeds:
1. Wear work gloves to protect your hands.
2. Rub dry umbels vigorously between your hands or against a wire kitchen sieve.
3. This friction breaks off the spiny hairs: this is called **debearding**.
4. Seeds separate smoothly, ready for sowing.
pages.illustration_description: Gloved hands rubbing dry umbels against a mesh sieve.

pages.title: Winnowing and airtight storage
pages.text:
To finish cleaning:
1. Pour debearded seeds into a flat bowl or calabash.
2. Blow gently or winnow in a light breeze to blow away dust and chaff.
3. Store clean seeds in an airtight jar with a small sachet of dry wood ash.
4. Label with variety and harvest year.
5. 🌱 Carrot seeds retain strong germination power for **4 to 5 years**.
pages.illustration_description: Airtight labeled jar with seeds and germination test plate.

pages.title: Congratulations! You master carrot seed saving
pages.text:
Well done! You now possess a rare and valuable skill among market gardeners: autonomous production of top quality carrot seeds!  
Season after season, you improve your variety to become sweeter, tougher, and perfectly adapted to your land.

Key takeaways:
- ✅ Select tropical/oriental varieties adapted to warm climates.
- ✅ Dig up 30 to 50 roots to inspect shape, color and taste.
- ✅ Dip cut root tips in ash before replanting.
- ✅ Isolate 500 m to 1 km from wild carrots.
- ✅ Harvest primary brown umbels and rub through a sieve to debeard.
pages.illustration_description: Proud market gardener displaying carrot harvest and seeds.
